from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Vectors are directed segments in space.",
            "The Right-Hand Rule defines 3D orientation.",
            "The cross product creates a perpendicular vector."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Conceptual Foundations", lecture_lines)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Fade in two vectors in #FFFFFF. Label them #FF0000.
        v1 = Vector([1, 1, 0], color=WHITE)
        v2 = Vector([1.5, -0.5, 0], color=WHITE)
        l1 = Text("v1", color="#FF0000", font_size=20)
        l2 = Text("v2", color="#FF0000", font_size=20)
        
        self.place_at_grid(v1, "B2")
        self.place_at_grid(v2, "B3")
        self.place_at_grid(l1, "B1")
        self.place_at_grid(l2, "B4")
        
        self.play(FadeIn(v1), FadeIn(v2), FadeIn(l1), FadeIn(l2))
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FF0000"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Show dot product result as a scalar value. Label #00FF00.
        dot_res = Text("v1 · v2 = scalar", color="#00FF00", font_size=24)
        self.place_at_grid(dot_res, "D3")
        
        self.play(Write(dot_res))
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#00FF00"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Illustrate vector projection visually with a dotted line #FFFF00.
        proj = DashedLine(v1.get_end(), v2.get_end(), color="#FFFF00")
        self.play(Create(proj))
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("2D 'Cross Product' as Oriented Area", [
            "The 2D cross product measures oriented area.",
            "A parallelogram forms between two vectors.",
            "Counter-clockwise sequences yield positive results."
        ])
        
        # Setup objects
        v1 = Vector([1, 0], color=WHITE)
        v2 = Vector([0, 1], color=WHITE)
        label_v1 = MathTex(r"\vec{v}_1", color=RED).next_to(v1.get_end(), RIGHT)
        label_v2 = MathTex(r"\vec{v}_2", color=RED).next_to(v2.get_end(), UP)
        
        parallelogram = Polygon(
            ORIGIN, v1.get_end(), v1.get_end() + v2.get_end(), v2.get_end(),
            fill_opacity=0.5, color=PURPLE
        )
        
        det_text = MathTex(r"\det(M) = x_1y_2 - x_2y_1", color=TEAL)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(TEAL))
        self.place_at_grid(v1, "C3")
        self.place_at_grid(v2, "C3")
        self.add(v1, v2, label_v1, label_v2)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(PURPLE))
        self.place_at_grid(parallelogram, "C3", scale_factor=1.5)
        self.play(Create(parallelogram))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.place_at_grid(det_text, "E4")
        self.play(Write(det_text))
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The 3D Cross Product Mechanics", [
            "Extend to 3D using determinant expansion.",
            "Magnitude relates to sin of the angle.",
            "The result is a vector in 3D.",
            "Magnitude grows as base vectors separate.",
            "Propellers illustrate the resulting thrust vector."
        ])

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FF5555")
        axes = ThreeDAxes(x_range=[-2, 2], y_range=[-2, 2], z_range=[-2, 2], axis_config={"color": WHITE})
        axes.set_color(WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(axes, "B2", scale_factor=0.3)
        self.add(axes)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#55FF55")
        v1 = Arrow3D(start=ORIGIN, end=RIGHT+UP, color="#FF0000")
        v2 = Arrow3D(start=ORIGIN, end=LEFT+UP, color="#FF0000")
        self.place_at_grid(v1, "B2", scale_factor=0.3)
        self.place_at_grid(v2, "B2", scale_factor=0.3)
        self.add(v1, v2)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFFF55")
        v3 = Arrow3D(start=ORIGIN, end=OUT*1.5, color="#FFFF00")
        self.place_at_grid(v3, "B2", scale_factor=0.3)
        self.play(Create(v3))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color("#55FFFF")
        self.wait(1)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[4].set_color("#FF55FF")
        self.wait(1)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Cross products find surface normal vectors.",
            "Torque calculation is a primary application.",
            "Zero cross product means vectors are collinear."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Geometric Interpretations & Applications", lecture_lines)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Parallelogram / Normal vector concept
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FF00FF"))
        rect = Rectangle(width=2.5, height=1.5, color="#FF00FF", fill_opacity=0.3)
        self.place_at_grid(rect, 'C3')
        norm_vec = Arrow(start=self.grid['C3'], end=self.grid['B3'], color="#00FF00", buff=0)
        self.add(rect, norm_vec)
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Torque concept
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#00FF00"))
        wrench = Line(start=self.grid['E2'], end=self.grid['E5'], color=WHITE, stroke_width=6)
        force = Arrow(start=self.grid['E5'], end=self.grid['D5'], color="#FFFF00", buff=0)
        # Use a valid grid key instead of non-existent 'E3.5'
        wrench.move_to((self.grid['E3'] + self.grid['E4']) / 2)
        self.add(wrench, force)
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Collinear vectors
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))
        v1 = Arrow(start=self.grid['F3'], end=self.grid['F5'], color=WHITE, buff=0)
        v2 = Arrow(start=self.grid['F3'], end=self.grid['F4'], color=WHITE, buff=0)
        self.add(v1, v2)
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: Mastering the Cross Product: From 2D intuition to 3D mechanics

sections.title: Conceptual Foundations (Prerequisites)
sections.content: Define vectors as directed line segments. Introduce the 'Right-Hand Rule' as the fundamental constraint for 3D orientation. Briefly explain that while the dot product yields a scalar (projection), the cross product generates a new vector perpendicular to the original plane.
sections.example: Visualizing a clock hand: The vector points towards the center of the clock, representing the axis of rotation.

sections.title: 2D 'Cross Product' as Oriented Area
sections.content: Explain the 2D cross product (determinant of a 2x2 matrix). Crucially, frame this as the 'signed area' of a parallelogram formed by two vectors. If the sequence is counter-clockwise, the result is positive; clockwise results in negative.
sections.example: A robot arm in 2D space moving between vectors (1,0) and (0,1); the area is 1, representing the space swept by the arm.

sections.title: The 3D Cross Product Mechanics
sections.content: Extend to 3D using the determinant expansion (i, j, k unit vectors). Emphasize that the magnitude |a × b| = |a||b|sin(θ). Use a 3D animation showing the resulting vector 'growing' out of the plane as the angle between the two base vectors changes.
sections.example: A spinning propeller blade: The two vectors are the blade length and the spin force; the cross product represents the resulting thrust vector pushing the aircraft forward.

sections.title: Geometric Interpretations & Applications
sections.content: Summarize the utility: 1. Finding a normal vector to a surface (essential for computer graphics lighting). 2. Calculating torque in physics. Reinforce that if the cross product is zero, vectors are collinear.
sections.example: A monkey turning a wrench: The force applied to the handle (vector 1) at a distance from the bolt (vector 2) creates a torque vector (cross product) that drives the bolt into the wall.
